$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t)-1,\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation, we get the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{{field-1}}={{field-2}} \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-2=-{X}_{1}(s)+3{X}_{2}(s)-{{field-3}}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}$ are the Laplace transforms of the functions ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t),$ respectively.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we compute the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}L{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)}=L{{x}_{1}(t)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)} \\ L{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)}=L{-{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t)-1}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}sL{{x}_{1}(t)}-{x}_{1}(0)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}+2L{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)} \\ sL{{x}_{2}(t)}-{x}_{2}(0)=-L{{x}_{1}(t)}+3L{{x}_{2}(t)}-L{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the results

$$
L{1}=\frac{1}{s},\,L{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+9},
$$

we can write our system as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)={X}_{1}(s)+\frac{2s}{{s}^{2}+9} \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-2=-{X}_{1}(s)+3{X}_{2}(s)-\frac{1}{s}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}$ are the Laplace transforms of the functions ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t),$ respectively.
